# id: # kind is false-positive or false-negative; status is open or closed.

description: Fixed by formal-mode-aware call scanning; covered by verification_diff_modular_call.adb.

Redundant_Boolean_Comparison fired on a same-named enumeration literal instead of Standard.True/False; fixed by requiring the non-literal operand's type to resolve to Standard.Boolean; covered by redundant_boolean_comparison_clean.adb.

Dead_Store, Overwritten_Assignment, and Repeated_Statement fired on Volatile/Atomic/Address-clause objects (memory-mapped hardware registers), where a write is observable on its own and does not need a later Ada-level read; fixed by an Is_Externally_Observable exemption in Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Data_Flow; covered by volatile_register_writes_clean.adb.

Global_Contract_Mismatch (and related Global/Depends/SPARK-readiness checks) fired on declarations with no SPARK_Mode aspect of their own nested inside a package/subprogram/task/protected body or spec marked SPARK_Mode => Off, because Effective_SPARK_Enabled only inspected the declaration itself and never walked up to the enclosing scope that the mode is inherited from; fixed by adding that lexical walk in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Dependency_Analysis, Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness, and Adalang_Analyzer.Flow_Interp; reproduced against AdaCore/spark2014 Tokeneer example, alarm-interfac.adb; covered by spark_mode_off_global_clean.adb.

Uninitialized_Output did not credit an out-mode parameter as initialized when the write happened inside a called nested subprogram whose own Global contract declares Output/In_Out mode on that variable as an up-level global, because Statement_Writes_Parameter only scanned actual parameters passed at the call site and never consulted the callee's own Global contract; fixed by adding Callee_Writes_Global in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness; reproduced against AdaCore/spark2014 Tokeneer example, configdata.adb (ValidateFile / ReadLatchUnlock and siblings); covered by uninitialized_output_nested_call_clean.adb.

Depends_Contract_Mismatch, Incomplete_Depends_Contract, and Missing_Depends_Contract mishandled combined-output Depends syntax "(A, B) => C": Ada's own aggregate grammar has no comma-separated choice list (only "|" separates discrete choices), so Libadalang parses the parenthesized designator list as a nested positional aggregate rather than as separate identifier designators; every affected check only recognized a designator that was itself a plain identifier, so both outputs were silently dropped and the shared input was misreported as unused ("listed after null"); fixed by expanding the nested aggregate's own associations in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Dependency_Analysis.Parse_Depends and Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Collect_Depends_Outputs; reproduced against AdaCore/spark2014 Tokeneer example, configdata.adb (ReadDuration); covered by depends_combined_output_clean.adb.

Uninitialized_Output flagged composite (record- or array-typed) out parameters that were fully initialized field-by-field or element-by-element, because Same_Parameter only recognized a plain identifier as referring to the tracked parameter, not a selected component (Param.Field := ...) or an indexed/sliced name (Param (I) := ...); fixed by walking down through nested Dotted_Name and Call_Expr prefixes to the innermost identifier in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Same_Parameter; reproduced against AdaCore/spark2014 Tokeneer example, admin.adb (Logon), cert-attr-auth.adb and siblings (Extract); covered by uninitialized_output_composite_clean.adb. A remaining case (auditlog.adb, SetFileDetails) writes an array through a for-loop over its full index range rather than by literal index or field name; proving that covers every index would require reasoning about loop bounds matching the array's index subtype, a materially harder problem left open (see quality/external_corpus_findings.md).

Uninitialized_Output flagged an out parameter forwarded positionally to another overload of the same subprogram name, when several overloads shared the same parameter count and modes (a common shape for a family of Encode/Decode procedures differing only in one parameter's type): Call.P_Call_Params demands one fully precise overload resolution for the whole call and returns nothing when that fails, and the per-actual fallback Assoc.P_Get_Params (Imprecise_Fallback => True) can itself raise in the same heavily-overloaded scenario; fixed in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Statement_Writes_Parameter by falling back, for a purely positional actual, to resolving only the callee name (a more lenient operation that still succeeds) and pairing by literal position via the new Callee_Formal_At_Position; reproduced against cubesatlab/cubedos, cubedos-lib-xdr.adb (the Encode family); covered by uninitialized_output_overloaded_forward_clean.adb. A distinct, narrower case remained open: a scalar written unconditionally inside a `for` loop with statically non-empty bounds and no early exit was still treated as possibly-unwritten, because every loop kind was conservatively assumed to be skippable; closed as FP-009.

Uninitialized_Output flagged a scalar out parameter written unconditionally inside a `for` loop with a statically non-empty range (e.g. `for I in 1 .. 3 loop ... Value := ...; end loop;`), because every loop kind was conservatively treated as possibly executing zero times; fixed in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Interpret_Initialization by special-casing `for` loops: when the iteration range's bounds are statically known (via Adalang_Analyzer.Flow_Eval.Choice_Interval) and non-empty, and the loop body contains no exit/return/raise/goto anywhere (the new Contains_Loop_Escape), the body's own computed initialization result is trusted instead of discarded, since nothing can leave the loop before finishing a pass; while/plain loops and any `for` loop containing an early exit remain conservatively unresolved, to avoid trading this false positive for a false negative; found in cubedos-lib-xdr.adb's Encode family (the loop-based writes remaining after FP-008); verified with a fixture faithfully copying that loop shape rather than a fresh live re-run of the checkout; covered by uninitialized_output_static_loop_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_output_static_loop_early_exit.adb (still flags with an early exit present). This fix as originally landed introduced a false-negative regression on array parameters, because Same_Parameter's coarse whole-object treatment of "Arr (I) := ..." (see FP-007) let a write to just one index of a partial-range loop through the same trust condition; closed together with the array-loop-coverage case as FP-010 before any external report.

Following FP-009, a for-loop over a statically non-empty, escape-free range whose body wrote an array out-parameter through a single indexed write (e.g. `Arr (I) := ...;`) was trusted as fully initializing the whole array regardless of whether the loop's range actually covered every index, because Same_Parameter cannot distinguish "wrote one element" from "wrote every element"; caught by testing a 3-element array against a `for I in 1 .. 2 loop` before this shipped externally. Fixed in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Interpret_Initialization by restricting the FP-009 trust path to non-array parameters and adding a separate, independent proof for arrays: the new Array_Index_Type resolves Param's own array-index subtype, Loop_Covers_Index_Range recognizes exactly two shapes whose iteration domain is provably that whole index range ("for I in Index_Type loop", a bare subtype mark naming the same index subtype, or "for I in Param'Range loop", whose coverage holds by construction independent of actual bounds), and List_Always_Writes_Loop_Index / Statement_Always_Writes_Loop_Index confirm the body unconditionally writes "Param (I)" indexed by exactly that control variable, recursing through if/case alternatives (an "if" with no "else" cannot be unconditional) the same way Interpret_Initialization's own Merge logic does; this also finally closes the FP-007-documented Tokeneer SetFileDetails case ("for I in LogFileIndexT loop LogFileEntries (I) := ...; end loop;") and the general array-loop-coverage limitation left open by FP-007/FP-009. An explicit "Low .. High" literal range that happens to match the array's bounds is deliberately left unrecognized (narrower in scope than the subtype-mark/'Range shapes, which need no bound arithmetic at all). Covered by uninitialized_output_array_loop_subtype_clean.adb and uninitialized_output_array_loop_range_attribute_clean.adb (clean), and uninitialized_output_array_loop_partial_range.adb and uninitialized_output_array_loop_range_attribute_early_exit.adb (still flag).

Uninitialized_Output flagged an out parameter written as "Subp_Name.Param := ...;" inside "procedure Subp_Name (Param : out ...)", where Subp_Name is the enclosing subprogram's own name used to qualify Param (Ada's general unit-name qualification, RM 8.3), typically to disambiguate from a same-named private component of an enclosing protected or task object that would otherwise shadow Param for simple-name visibility; Same_Parameter's prefix-unwrap loop always inspected the Dotted_Name's prefix ("Subp_Name") and discarded the suffix ("Param"), so it looked at the wrong identifier and concluded the parameter was never written. Fixed in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Same_Parameter by checking, before the existing unwrap loop, whether the suffix matches Param's name and the prefix resolves to the new Enclosing_Subprogram_Or_Entry (the nearest enclosing Subp_Body or Entry_Body) -- a narrow, additive check that requires an exact match to the specific enclosing construct, so an unrelated same-named field access on a genuinely different parameter (e.g. "R.Size := ...;" where R is a different out/in-out parameter) is unaffected. Found via a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation run -P-less scan of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended): confirmed in aws-server-push.adb's protected body Waiter_Information (procedure Info, 4 parameters), Shutdown_If_Empty (Open), and Get (Queue) -- 6 of that file's 16 Uninitialized_Output findings, verified by diffing the exact same file's output before and after the fix. Covered by uninitialized_output_own_name_qualifier_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_output_own_name_qualifier_guard.adb (still flags the unrelated-object case).

Uninitialized_Output flagged an out parameter forwarded as a named actual (e.g. "Size => Size") to a protected operation whose formals include one typed Ada.Calendar.Time, because Libadalang's Assoc.P_Get_Params (Imprecise_Fallback => True) fails to classify the actual at all in that shape (a formal typed Ada.Calendar.Time on an otherwise-unambiguous protected-operation call seems sufficient on its own to trip it; root cause is a Libadalang resolution limitation, not investigated further), and the FP-008 fallback (Callee_Formal_At_Position) only ever applied to purely positional actuals (Assoc.F_Designator = null), so a named actual hitting this gap had no fallback at all and was silently never recognized as a write. Fixed in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Statement_Writes_Parameter by adding the new Callee_Formal_By_Name (the named-actual counterpart to Callee_Formal_At_Position: same lenient callee-name-only resolution, matching by the designator's own name instead of by position) and using it whenever Assoc.F_Designator is not null. Found immediately after FP-011 in the very same aws-server-push.adb wrapper procedure "Info" (the outer, non-protected one forwarding to Waiter_Information.Info) while confirming that fix hadn't left a related gap open; reproduced with a minimal, non-generic 44-line fixture built by bisecting the real file (isolated to: a protected operation, 4 out-mode formals, one typed Ada.Calendar.Time, forwarded by named actual from an outer wrapper) after two closer, hand-written syntheses of the shape failed to reproduce it. A guard fixture confirms a named actual naming a genuinely "in" formal on a callee hitting the same resolution gap is not mistaken for writing an unrelated "out" parameter that is never forwarded. Covered by uninitialized_output_named_actual_forward_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_output_named_actual_forward_guard.adb (still flags the unrelated-parameter case).

Uninitialized_Output flagged an out parameter initialized solely via a parameterless prefixed procedure call (e.g. "Queue.Clear;", forwarding to Ada.Containers.Ordered_Maps.Clear), because such a call has no Call_Expr node -- Libadalang represents "Object.Operation;" as a bare Dotted_Name -- and Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Statement_Writes_Parameter only ever inspected Ada_Call_Expr call statements, the same gap already fixed for Wrong_Parameter_Mode and Dead_Store in Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Declarations.Parameter_Is_Written but left open here. Fixed in Statement_Writes_Parameter by adding an Ada_Dotted_Name branch that reuses Same_Parameter directly on the call node: its existing prefix-unwrap loop already reaches past the Dotted_Name's suffix (the method name) to the prefix, so no new unwrap logic was needed. Found in a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation re-run of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended) while investigating the residual Uninitialized_Output findings FP-011/FP-012 had left open in aws-server-push.adb: procedure Unregister_Clients's "Queue : out Tables.Map" is initialized only by "Queue.Clear;"; confirmed by diffing the file's own Uninitialized_Output output before and after the fix -- exactly that one finding disappeared, nothing new appeared, and the corpus-wide total dropped by exactly one. The other two residual Uninitialized_Output findings in the same file (Get_Data's "Data", Send's "Queue") were reviewed and are genuine: real paths (an empty chunk list; an early return before "Queue.Clear;") reach a normal return without ever writing the parameter, not analyzer mistakes. Covered by uninitialized_output_prefixed_clear_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_output_prefixed_clear_guard.adb (a second, unrelated out parameter left unwritten by the same call must still be flagged).

Wrong_Parameter_Mode recommended mode "out" for an in-out parameter written only through a selected component, indexed component, or slice of it (e.g. "State.Values (Index) := Value;"), because Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Declarations.Parameter_Is_Written's Assign_Stmt case delegated to Write_Target_Contains_Parameter, which deliberately unwraps any depth of nested selector/index to credit the base object as written -- correct for Dead_Store and Uninitialized_Output's coarser "was this touched at all" questions, but wrong for a mode-change recommendation: "out" formally disclaims any need for the incoming value, while a write to only part of a parameter inherently depends on every untouched part already holding a meaningful prior value. Found in a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation re-run of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended) while investigating the corpus's 126 Wrong_Parameter_Mode findings: 70 of them were AWS.Config.Set's single-field config setters (e.g. procedure Accept_Queue_Size, body "O.P (Accept_Queue_Size).Pos_Value := Value;"), each writing one element of Object's many-element parameter array while leaving every other configuration value untouched -- an in-out usage by construction, not a candidate for out. Fixed by adding Parameter_Is_Wholly_Written, identical to Parameter_Is_Written except its Assign_Stmt case requires the destination to be the parameter itself (Parameter_Name_Matches, no unwrap) rather than any nested selector/index reaching it, and using it (instead of the existing, still-unchanged Parameter_Is_Written) to gate only the "is only written; use mode out" recommendation in Analyze_Subprogram; the "is only read; use mode in" recommendation, Dead_Store, and Uninitialized_Output are unaffected. Confirmed against the real corpus: Wrong_Parameter_Mode findings dropped from 126 to 54 -- all 70 in aws-config-set.adb plus 2 more of the identical shape elsewhere (AWS.Net.Generic_Sets.Set_Data's "Set.Set (Index).Data := Data;", AWS.Client.HTTP_Utils.Decrement_Authentication_Attempt's "Counter (Level) := @ - 1;") -- with no new findings appearing anywhere. Covered by wrong_parameter_mode_partial_write_clean.adb (clean) and wrong_parameter_mode_partial_write_guard.adb (a direct, whole-object assignment must still be flagged).

Uninitialized_Read flagged a local scalar variable's own initializing assignment as a read of itself whenever the assignment's expression also mentioned an unrelated object's attribute of the same spelling (e.g. "Last := Fixed.Index (Data (First .. Data'Last), ...);", where the attribute designator "Last" in "Data'Last" has nothing to do with the local variable Last), because Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Data_Flow.Matches_Declaration -- shared read/write-detection infrastructure used by Uninitialized_Read, Dead_Store, and other data-flow checks -- falls back to a spelling-only comparison whenever semantic resolution fails, and Libadalang's own resolution correctly returns null for an attribute designator (it is syntactically an identifier but never refers to a declaration), which fed straight into that fallback. "First" and "Last" are two of the most common variable names for tracking string/array bounds, making this an easy, frequent collision with the identically-spelled standard attributes. Fixed by adding an early check in Matches_Declaration: an identifier that is specifically the F_Attribute child of its parent Attribute_Ref (not merely appearing somewhere inside one, so a genuine reference used as an attribute *prefix*, e.g. "Last'Size" where Last really is the tracked variable, is unaffected) never matches any declaration. Found in a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation re-run of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended) while investigating the corpus's Uninitialized_Read findings; reproduced with a minimal fixture before touching the fix, confirming the collision and that a differently-named variable does not trigger it. Confirmed against the real corpus: Uninitialized_Read findings dropped from 39 to 35 (aws-headers-values.adb, aws-log.adb, aws-config-ini.adb, aws-config-utils.adb, one each), with no new findings appearing anywhere and no change to any other check's totals in this corpus. Covered by uninitialized_read_attribute_designator_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_read_attribute_designator_guard.adb (a genuine attribute-prefix reference to the tracked variable must still be flagged).

Dead_Store flagged a write through an object-renaming declaration whose renamed object is part of a longer-lived parameter or global (e.g. "Info : Error_Details renames Self.Error_Detail;" where Self is an in-out parameter, then "Info := Some_Error;") as a dead store whenever "Info" itself was never read again by name within the same subprogram, even though the write is really to Self.Error_Detail -- observable by the caller after return and by any other code that later reads Self.Error_Detail directly. Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Control_Flow.Is_Local_To_Subprogram, the lexical-scope test Dead_Store uses to decide whether a written declaration is purely local, considers a renaming declaration "local" whenever it is textually nested inside the subprogram, regardless of what it aliases; and Data_Flow.Ultimate_Object (used by Assigned_Declaration to resolve a bare "Info := ...;" target) only follows a renamed object that is itself a bare identifier ("Y renames X;"), not one reached through a selected component, indexed component, or dereference, so it never unwound "Self.Error_Detail" back to Self's own (non-local, non-Object_Decl) declaration. Fixed by adding Renames_Nonlocal_Object in Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Control_Flow: walks the renamed object down through any depth of selected/indexed component or dereference (the same coarse, whichever-depth-only-the-base-object-matters treatment already used elsewhere in this project, e.g. Same_Parameter) to its base identifier, and disqualifies Decl from Dead_Store whenever that base is not itself local to Subprogram. A renaming of a genuinely local object's field is unaffected. Found in a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation re-run of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended) while investigating the corpus's Dead_Store findings: 13 of the 23 were concentrated in a single file, aws-http2-stream.adb, all of this exact shape. Confirmed against the real corpus: Dead_Store findings dropped from 23 to 10, all 13 in aws-http2-stream.adb, with no new findings appearing anywhere. Covered by dead_store_renaming_of_parameter_field_clean.adb (clean) and dead_store_renaming_of_parameter_field_guard.adb (a renaming of a genuinely local object's field must still be flagged).

Uninitialized_Read flagged a scalar local variable's read inside a nested subprogram or entry body as happening before that variable's genuine initializing write elsewhere in the enclosing subprogram, whenever the nested body's own declaration was textually positioned earlier than the write, even though the nested body is only actually invoked (and its read only actually reached) after that write runs. Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Data_Flow.First_Access is a plain pre-order AST walk with no notion of actual call order: a nested subprogram body is a declaration, elaborated but not executed at its own textual position, yet the walk recursed into it exactly like any other statement, discovering a read inside it before ever reaching a later statement of the enclosing subprogram that writes the same variable. Found in a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation re-run of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended) while investigating the 5 Uninitialized_Read findings FP-015 had left open in aws-headers-values.adb: Split's nested function To_Set calls Next_Value (whose out-mode formals initialize To_Set's own locals Name_First, Name_Last, Value_First, Value_Last) before ever invoking its own nested function Element, which reads those locals as up-level references; Element's declaration, though, textually precedes that Next_Value call. The same shape affected Split itself over First (read inside To_Set, textually preceding Split's own initializing assignment to First). Fixed by skipping recursion into a child node of kind Ada_Subp_Body or Ada_Entry_Body during First_Access's walk; this trades away detecting a genuine read through a nested body invoked before the tracked variable's initialization (unrecognized, not soundly ruled out) for not flagging the common, correct case, consistent with this project's general bias toward fewer false positives. Confirmed against the real corpus: Uninitialized_Read findings dropped from 35 (the count after FP-015/FP-016) to 29 -- 7 instances across aws-net-acceptors.adb, aws-url-set.adb, and aws-headers-values.adb disappeared, and one previously-hidden, separate finding in aws-net-acceptors.adb (a different variable, unrelated root cause) was exposed by no longer stopping the scan early -- see the "still open" note in external_corpus_findings.md. Covered by uninitialized_read_nested_subprogram_order_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_read_nested_subprogram_order_guard.adb (a genuine direct read in the enclosing subprogram's own statements, near an unrelated nested subprogram, must still be flagged).

Uninitialized_Read flagged a scalar local variable as read before assignment even when it was genuinely initialized by being forwarded (positionally or by name) as an out/in-out actual to a callee whose per-actual resolution Libadalang's own Assoc.P_Get_Params (Imprecise_Fallback => True) fails to classify -- the same resolution fragility already fixed for Uninitialized_Output's write detection in FP-008/FP-012 (a formal typed Ada.Calendar.Time on an otherwise-unambiguous call is one confirmed trigger; heavy overload is another), but Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Data_Flow.Call_Writes_Declaration and Call_Reads_Simple_Actual -- the corresponding read/write detection Uninitialized_Read's First_Access uses -- had no equivalent fallback: when P_Get_Params found nothing, the actual was silently treated as neither read nor written, and the scan continued past the real initializing call to whatever came next, misreporting that as the first access. Fixed by adding Callee_Formal_At_Position, Callee_Formal_By_Name, and Formal_Mode to Checks.Data_Flow (duplicating, not sharing, the equivalent functions already in SPARK_Readiness, consistent with this project's existing per-module-helper style) and using them, exactly as Statement_Writes_Parameter already does, whenever P_Get_Params resolves no formal at all for a given actual. Found in a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation re-run of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended) while investigating the aws-net-acceptors.adb finding FP-017 had exposed: confirmed, in isolation, that the same Ada.Calendar.Time-formal trigger already known from FP-012 also breaks Call_Writes_Declaration (reproduced with a minimal fixture derived from the FP-012 shape before touching the fix). Confirmed against the real corpus: one instance disappeared, aws-session.adb's Get_Value (Found, forwarded positionally to Get_Node). The aws-net-acceptors.adb finding that motivated this investigation remained after FP-018 because even Callee_Formal_At_Position's callee-name resolution failed in the deeper full-batch provider context; it was subsequently closed as FP-019. Covered by uninitialized_read_positional_forward_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_read_positional_forward_guard.adb (a variable never forwarded at all, at the same resolution-fragile callee shape, must still be flagged).

Uninitialized_Read flagged AWS.Net.Acceptors.Get's Error local in the 273-file no-project batch even though Sets.Is_Read_Ready initializes it through an out actual; explicitly supplying the root/parent units made Libadalang unable to resolve P_Get_Params, the whole callee, its called-subprogram spec, or even the instantiated package prefix, so the existing FP-018 fallback could not determine a formal mode. Fixed by adding Unknown_Access to Data_Flow.First_Access: a simple actual at an unresolved call is a terminal unknown boundary, because the call may initialize it, rather than No_Access that lets the scan continue and later claim a read definitely preceded every write. Resolved in/out/in-out calls retain their existing classifications. Covered by uninitialized_read_unresolved_call_clean.adb and uninitialized_read_unresolved_call_guard.adb; confirmed on the minimized six-file AWS trigger and original 273-file invocation, where all three aws-net-acceptors.adb instances disappeared and corpus Uninitialized_Read findings fell from 28 to 4.

Project-scale --verify on pinned AdaCore/aws classified 265 initialization obligations as Definite_Error, including a String renaming, default-initialized private/composite objects, composite out parameters used for bounds or as write targets, and scalar address overlays. Fixed in Adalang_Analyzer.Flow_Interp by propagating simple-renaming state, reserving definite-uninitialized seeding for resolved scalar declarations/out parameters, treating address-clause objects conservatively, and excluding non-value attribute uses and assignment-target base names from initialization reads. The guard still classifies a rename of a genuinely uninitialized scalar as Definite_Error. Covered by verification_initialization_defaults_clean.adb and verification_initialization_rename_error.adb; confirmed against the same pinned 348-file AWS project, where Definite_Error fell from 265 to 0.

Uninitialized_Output (and, duplicated, Uninitialized_Read) flagged an out parameter forwarded positionally to a same-named sibling overload whenever one of the overloads carried a System.Address-typed formal: Call.F_Name.P_Referenced_Decl (Imprecise_Fallback => True) resolved the call back to the *enclosing* (narrower) overload itself rather than the sibling actually being called, so Callee_Formal_At_Position's existing lenient lookup (added for FP-008) found a real, non-null callee whose own formal list simply did not reach the actual's position, and silently returned nothing rather than falling back further. A further instance of the resolution fragility already worked around for FP-008/FP-012/FP-018/FP-019. Fixed by adding Callee_Candidate_By_Arity to Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness (and, duplicated, Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Data_Flow): when the directly-resolved callee's spec does not actually contain a formal at the sought position/name, search every same-named candidate in scope (Name.P_All_Env_Elements) for one whose total formal count matches the call's actual count, trying spec-kind candidates before body-kind ones so one real subprogram's spec-and-body pair (both returned by P_All_Env_Elements) is never double-counted as two same-arity candidates -- P_Canonical_Part, the natural way to deduplicate that pair, was tried first and rejected: it does not reliably map a body back to its own spec for this exact same-name-overload-plus-System.Address shape, the same underlying Libadalang confusion this function exists to route around. Reproduced against AdaCore/Ada_Drivers_Library, components/src/radio/hm11/hm11.adb's Transmit_And_Check (a 6-formal overload forwarding Status positionally to a 4-formal sibling missing an Address-typed Received formal from the caller's own perspective); confirmed against the real corpus (hal/src + components/src, 133 files, --recommended): Uninitialized_Output fell from 131 to 74. Covered by uninitialized_output_overload_arity_fallback_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_output_overload_arity_fallback_guard.adb (a second out parameter never forwarded at all, at the same shape, must still be flagged).

Uninitialized_Read flagged the first Ada-level mention of a scalar local declared with the Import aspect (e.g. "L : Character with Import, Address => Buffer_Addr;", an overlay onto a buffer some other layer -- DMA, a driver call -- already populated) as a read-before-assignment, even though such an object is defined to get its value from outside the Ada code and needs no explicit initializer. Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Declarations.Analyze_Object_Declaration's Uninitialized_Read gate checked only F_Default_Expr, F_Renaming_Clause, and scalar-ness, with no aspect exemption, unlike Dead_Store/Overwritten_Assignment/Repeated_Statement, which already exempt Volatile/Atomic/Address-aspected declarations via Data_Flow.Is_Externally_Observable (FP-003) -- and every observed Import overlay also carries an Address aspect (Import alone needs somewhere to import from), so that existing, already-vetted test applies directly. Fixed by adding "and then not Data_Flow.Is_Externally_Observable (Decl.As_Basic_Decl)" to the same gate; no new aspect-detection code was needed. Reproduced against AdaCore/Ada_Drivers_Library; this exact overlay shape accounted for 12 of the corpus's 20 Uninitialized_Read findings (10 in components/src/radio/hm11/hm11.adb, 2 in components/src/radio/si4432/si4432.adb); confirmed against the real corpus (hal/src + components/src, 133 files, --recommended): Uninitialized_Read fell from 20 to 8. Covered by uninitialized_read_import_overlay_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_read_import_overlay_guard.adb (an ordinary scalar with no externally-observable aspect must still be flagged).

Uninitialized_Read missed a genuine initializing write made through an out-mode actual of a function called for its return value inside a larger expression (e.g. "Nb_Touch := This.I2C_Read (Reg, Status);", an ordinary Ada function with an out parameter, called within an assignment's RHS rather than as its own call statement), and instead flagged a later, unrelated read of the same variable as the first access. Data_Flow.First_Access's own Ada_Assign_Stmt case only checked whether the tracked declaration was read anywhere in the RHS (correctly excluding it, since Reads_Declaration's Call_Expr handling already recognizes an out-mode actual as not a read) or was the assignment's own simple destination -- but every path through that case returns unconditionally, so it never falls through to the generic child recursion below, where the Ada_Call_Expr case that would recognize the nested call itself as a write actually lives; the write was silently dropped as No_Access and the scan continued to the next real access. Fixed in Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Data_Flow.First_Access by delegating to First_Access itself, recursively, over just Stmt.F_Expr whenever neither the read nor the simple-destination-write case matches, giving the RHS's own nested call expression the same chance at Ada_Call_Expr-based write recognition any other call statement already gets. Reproduced against AdaCore/Ada_Drivers_Library; this shape (a driver's Check_Id-style helper calling This.I2C_Read/SPAD_Info as a function) accounted for 7 of the corpus's residual Uninitialized_Read findings after FP-022 (components/src/range_sensor/VL53L0X/vl53l0x.adb, components/src/touch_panel/ft6x06/ft6x06.adb x3, components/src/touch_panel/ft5336/ft5336.adb x3); confirmed against the real corpus (hal/src + components/src, 133 files, --recommended): Uninitialized_Read fell from 8 to 1. Covered by uninitialized_read_function_out_actual_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_read_function_out_actual_guard.adb (a variable never forwarded to the function at all, at the same call-in-expression shape, must still be flagged).

Uninitialized_Read flagged a local scalar's own initializing assignment as a read of itself whenever a function called on the RHS with named actuals had a formal whose designator happened to share the local's spelling (e.g. "New_X := To_Integer_16 (LSB => Buffer (0), MSB => Buffer (1));", where the local "LSB : Float" is unrelated to To_Integer_16's own "LSB" formal), the same general shape as the attribute-designator collision already fixed for Uninitialized_Read (FP-015) but for a named-actual designator instead of an attribute name. Reads_Declaration's Ada_Call_Expr case only specially handles a Param_Assoc whose F_R_Expr is itself a plain identifier; when the actual expression is not a bare identifier (here, "Buffer (0)"), it falls back to a fully generic recursive walk over the whole Param_Assoc node, which visits every child indiscriminately -- including F_Designator (the formal's own name, "LSB") right alongside F_R_Expr (the actual expression) -- and Matches_Declaration's existing spelling-based fallback (already documented as a deliberate tradeoff in FP-015) then matched the designator by pure text. Fixed by adding an early check to Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Data_Flow.Matches_Declaration, mirroring the existing attribute-designator one: an identifier that is specifically the F_Designator child of its parent Param_Assoc never matches any declaration, regardless of Libadalang's own resolution outcome for it, since a formal designator could never legitimately denote a locally tracked object. Reproduced against AdaCore/Ada_Drivers_Library, components/src/motion/bno055/bosch_bno055.adb's Output; confirmed against the real corpus (hal/src + components/src, 133 files, --recommended): Uninitialized_Read fell from 1 to 0. Covered by uninitialized_read_named_actual_designator_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_read_named_actual_designator_guard.adb (a local genuinely passed as the actual expression, not just sharing the designator's spelling, must still be flagged when read before assignment).

Wrong_Parameter_Mode recommended mode "in" for an in-out parameter that was, in fact, written -- forwarded to another out/in-out formal through a function called for its return value inside a larger expression (e.g. "Result := Statement_Initialization (..., Bad_Return);", where Bad_Return is Statement_Initialization's own in-out formal) -- because Checks.Declarations.Parameter_Is_Written's Ada_Assign_Stmt case checked only whether the assignment's own destination contained Param, and that whole case always returns without ever falling through to the generic child recursion below where the Ada_Call_Expr case that would recognize the nested call as a write actually lives; Parameter_Is_Read's own Ada_Assign_Stmt case already recurses into the RHS correctly, so the parameter looked read-only. The same shape as FP-023 (Data_Flow.First_Access, for Uninitialized_Read), here in the sibling function serving Wrong_Parameter_Mode/Dead_Store's write detection instead. Found via this project's own --recommended self-analysis gate on its own source (Adalang_Analyzer.Subprogram_Summaries.List_Initialization's Bad_Return, added by the interprocedural-effect-summaries commit) rather than an external corpus. Fixed with the identical delegate-into-the-RHS pattern as FP-023, applied to both Parameter_Is_Written and its sibling Parameter_Is_Wholly_Written (FP-014), which shares the same unconditional-return structure. Covered by wrong_parameter_mode_call_in_expression_clean.adb (clean) and wrong_parameter_mode_call_in_expression_guard.adb (a parameter never forwarded at all, at the same call-in-expression shape, must still be flagged read-only).

Adalang_Analyzer.Subprogram_Summaries.Mark_Formal_Write's "when others => null;" handler tripped the project's own Empty_Exception_Handler/Exception_Swallowed checks under --recommended self-analysis, the same kind of self-inflicted regression already noted while fixing FP-008. Fixed by replacing it with a Log_Verbose_Once diagnostic, matching this file's own existing convention (Register_Body, Scan_Unit already do this). No fixture needed: this is a style regression in the analyzer's own source caught by its own self-analysis gate, not a defect in a check's logic.

Uninitialized_Output (and the duplicated Uninitialized_Read/Wrong_Parameter_Mode/Dead_Store fallback) missed reads and writes made through a call on an access-to-subprogram-typed component or discriminant (e.g. "This.Receive (Port, Received, Length, Status, Timeout, As_Stream);" where Receive is a "not null access procedure (...)" discriminant of This's own record type, not an ordinary subprogram name), because Callee_Formal_At_Position/Callee_Formal_By_Name resolved Call.F_Name back to the discriminant's own Component_Decl/Discriminant_Spec, whose P_Subp_Spec_Or_Null is null. Fixed in both SPARK_Readiness and Checks.Data_Flow by resolving the object's Type_Expr to its named or anonymous Type_Decl, recognizing its Access_To_Subp_Def, and using that definition's embedded Subp_Spec as the indirect callable profile before attempting the same-name arity fallback. Originally observed in AdaCore/Ada_Drivers_Library, components/src/radio/hm11/hm11.adb:1315, Read_Characteristic_UUID's "This.Receive (This.Port, This.Responce'Address, This.Responce'Length, Status, Timeout, As_Stream => True);". Covered across all four affected analyses by access_to_subprogram_actuals_clean.adb and by access_to_subprogram_actuals_guard.adb, which confirms an unrelated out parameter remains reported.

Uninitialized_Read flagged a scalar local variable at "pragma Unreferenced (X);", right after its own declaration, misclassifying it as a read before its first real assignment. Data_Flow.First_Access's plain pre-order child walk has no special case for a pragma: Matches_Declaration resolves the pragma argument identifier (via P_Referenced_Decl, since a pragma argument genuinely denotes the entity it names) back to X's own declaration, the same way an ordinary reference would, with no way to tell "this identifier is merely named by a compiler directive" from "this identifier's value is read here" -- unlike an executable pragma such as Assert, whose argument is a genuine boolean expression evaluated at that point. Fixed by adding an early check to Matches_Declaration, gated on the pragma's own name (not every pragma argument, so "pragma Assert (Is_Ready);" with a bare-identifier condition still counts as a read): an identifier that is the argument of a pragma Unreferenced, Unmodified, or Warnings never matches any declaration. Observed in the wild in AdaCore/Certyflie (parameter.adb, memory.adb, log.adb, each an identical "Has_Succeed : Boolean; pragma Unreferenced (Has_Succeed);" shape after a status-returning procedure's local); confirmed against the real corpus, Uninitialized_Read fell from 7 to 3 with no new findings appearing anywhere. Covered by uninitialized_read_pragma_unreferenced_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_read_pragma_unreferenced_guard.adb (a bare-identifier condition of pragma Assert, the same colliding shape but genuinely evaluated at runtime, must still be flagged).

A plain subtype of a scalar type from a with'd, externally defined package (e.g. "subtype T_Int16 is Interfaces.Integer_16;") makes Libadalang's own property implementation raise Property_Error ("dereferencing a null access") whenever ordinary semantic analysis needs that subtype's privacy/type, silently suppressing the checks that depend on the result. Confirmed via symbolic backtraces (temporary GNAT.Traceback.Symbolic instrumentation) from two structurally unrelated call sites, both bottoming out in the identical Libadalang chain inside vendored libadalang-implementation.adb: Subtype_Decl_P_Get_Type -> Base_Subtype_Decl_P_From_Type_Bound -> Base_Subtype_Decl_P_Is_Private -> Base_Type_Decl_P_Next_Part -> Raise_Property_Exception. The first site is Subprogram_Summaries.Register_Body's Body.P_Decl_Part, resolving a subprogram body's separately declared spec to build its interprocedural effect summary; when it fails, no summary is registered for that subprogram, so callers lose its May_Read/May_Write/May_Block/May_Raise effects for every check that consults summaries. The second is SPARK_Readiness.Check_Discriminant_Access's ordinary name resolution on an unrelated Dotted_Name, which is silently skipped for that node. This is an upstream Libadalang defect, not an AdaLang Analyzer logic error, and there is no fix available on this side of the boundary; both call sites already contain the failure correctly via their existing "when others" handler (skip and log via Log_Verbose_Once, keep going) rather than aborting the run, but the net effect is a real, currently open coverage gap. Originally observed in AdaCore/Certyflie, crazyflie_support/src/types.ads ("subtype T_Int32 is Interfaces.Integer_32;" and three siblings among its T_IntNN/T_UintNN block); reduced to a minimal single-file case. Covered by external_subtype_signature_match_robustness.adb and a CLI-robustness check in run_cli_robustness.sh confirming the run still completes and reports its unrelated, genuine Unused_Parameter finding rather than aborting. Re-investigated with an eye toward a local fix, with two further findings. First, Register_Body's own fallback (use Subprogram itself as the key declaration when P_Decl_Part fails) was unreachable for exactly this failure, because a Property_Error raised while elaborating a declare block's own declarative part is not handled by that block's own handlers (RM 11.2); it escaped past the intended narrow handler to Register_Body's coarser outer one, discarding the whole summary instead of falling back. Fixed by assigning Decl_Part in the executable part instead (a genuine, narrow correctness improvement, kept independently of this issue), but it does not close the gap: the fallback path (Declaration_Name on the body, which must itself mangle Foo's parameter types into a unique name) requires the identical broken property and fails the same way one step later, confirming no cheap workaround exists on this side. Second, the failure's true trigger has now been isolated and is fully deterministic (an earlier note here, since corrected, mistook inconsistent PATH exports across separate manual test invocations for genuine Libadalang non-determinism): both Libadalang.Auto_Provider (used for -P and project-less runs alike) and its Libadalang.Unit_Files.Default_Provider fallback resolve with'd units, including Interfaces, purely through GNATCOLL.Projects, which shells out to "gnatls -v" to locate the default runtime's predefined source path; -P only contributes source-file discovery via GPR2 and does not feed the project's own runtime into this lookup. Without a "gnatls" on PATH, the lookup finds nothing, Interfaces is entirely unresolved, and the property chain above dereferences null every time instead of degrading gracefully; with a real GNAT toolchain on PATH, the same binary against the same input never fails (confirmed 20/20 clean vs. 20/20 failing in controlled, single-shell-invocation batches). Since there is still no way to make the affected checks succeed without a real GNAT toolchain present, Adalang_Analyzer now warns at startup (Adalang_Analyzer_CLI, gated on Locate_Exec_On_Path ("gnatls")) so the condition is visible instead of a silent, scattered coverage gap; run_cli_robustness.sh's check tolerates either outcome, since it should pass regardless of whether the invoking environment happens to have a toolchain on PATH. Partial mitigation added: since "alr exec -- which gnatls" resolved a cached toolchain that bare PATH did not, most of the remaining exposure was invocations of an alr-built binary run directly instead of through "alr exec", not a genuinely toolchain-less machine. Adalang_Analyzer_CLI.Locate_Alire_Gnatls_Dir now reads Alire's own global settings.toml for the selected gnat toolchain and, when found, self-augments PATH with that toolchain's bin/ directory before the gnatls check runs, so this common case no longer needs "alr exec" wrapping at all (confirmed: the warning no longer fires and external_subtype_signature_match_robustness.adb resolves cleanly under a stripped PATH with only HOME set). This does not close the issue: a machine with no Alire-managed toolchain anywhere (e.g. a bare binary copied to a box that never ran "alr build" locally) still hits the underlying Libadalang defect exactly as described above.

Uninitialized_Read flagged a scalar local variable as read before assignment even though a plain "Decl := Expr;" wrote it earlier in the very same if-branch, whenever Libadalang's own semantic resolution had already failed elsewhere in the same subprogram (observed with the FP-029 Property_Error, but the mechanism applies to any resolution failure). Checks.Data_Flow.First_Access's Ada_Assign_Stmt case detected a write via "Assigned_Declaration (Node) = Decl", which calls P_Referenced_Decl on the destination identifier and compares the result to Decl by exact declaration identity, with no fallback; Referenced_Declaration's own blanket "when others => return No_Basic_Decl;" silently converts any Property_Error there into a non-match, so once resolution fails for one name in a declarative region, every later plain-identifier write in that same region goes undetected and First_Access reads straight past it to report the next successfully-resolved read as the first access -- while Reads_Declaration's sibling read-detection path already tolerates the identical resolution failure via Matches_Declaration's spelling-based fallback, so reads kept firing but writes silently stopped being recognized. Root-caused with temporary Ada.Text_IO/GNAT.Traceback instrumentation (reverted) confirming Referenced_Declaration raised the FP-029 Property_Error for essentially every name in Stabilizer_Alt_Hold_Update, including the plain locals in question. Fixed by replacing the exact-identity comparison with Matches_Declaration (Stmt.F_Dest, Decl) for a plain-identifier destination, giving write-detection the same resolution-failure fallback read-detection already had. Observed in the wild in AdaCore/Certyflie, stabilizer.adb's Stabilizer_Alt_Hold_Update (Prev_Integ at :355, Baro_V_Speed and Alt_Hold_PID_Out at :392); confirmed against the real corpus (crazyflie_support/src + src + the two Ada_Drivers_Library motion drivers, 88 files, --recommended): Uninitialized_Read fell from 3 to 0, with the full violation-count diff otherwise identical before and after. No fixture: this specific write-then-read shape resisted three separate synthetic reproduction attempts (a bare Interfaces-derived subtype, the same subtype with a use_type_clause and a consuming expression, and a from-scratch generic instantiation mirroring Pid's own record/range shape), the same "only reproduces in the original file's own multi-file context" difficulty already documented for FP-018/FP-019.

Bounded scalar verification (--verify) could report a Definite_Error initialization-check for an obligation that was genuinely only Unproved, when the same source location was visited more than once by Verify_Subprogram's CFG worklist fixed point before that fixed point had converged for the node in question -- typically across a loop header's back edge, whose contribution reaches a downstream merge point only after that point was already processed, and its outcome already recorded, using the loop's pre-back-edge, not-yet-joined state. Proof_Obligations.Register_At's Replaces function treats Definite_Error and Proved_Safe as terminal once recorded for a given stable ID (only Unreachable/Unsupported may supersede them), which is correct when two independent sound analyses reach different conclusions about the same location, but not when the "first" recording came from an intermediate, non-fixed-point-stable CFG state produced by the very same analysis pass: a later, fully-converged Unproved recording for the identical stable ID was then silently discarded instead of correcting it. Reproduced with a minimal fixture -- "for I in 1 .. Arg loop Val := I; end loop;" followed by a read of Val, where Arg is an ordinary Positive parameter, so the loop's range is dynamic but its lower bound guarantees at least one iteration -- for which Uninitialized_Read/Uninitialized_Output correctly found no violation (SPARK_Readiness's own initialization tracking is unaffected; this bug was confined to Verify_Subprogram's CFG fixed point in flow_interp.adb). Confirmed via temporary Record_Outcome instrumentation (reverted): the same stable ID recorded Definite_Error, then Unproved, then Definite_Error, then Unproved across Verify_Subprogram's two passes (Summary_Mode False, then True) for this one fixture, with the first (Definite_Error) value winning in the final report regardless of the later, correct Unproved recordings. Observed on real code in AdaCore/spark2014's Tokeneer corpus: msgproc.adb's GetStringByPos, ValFin at :66, the identical dynamic-for-loop-bound shape. Fixed by adding an optional Final parameter to Proof_Obligations.Register_At (default False, every existing call site unaffected) that always overwrites the current result for a stable ID, bypassing Replaces and the contradictory-result check, for producers that recompute a result once from a value known to be final; and by having Verify_Subprogram's Finalize_Node -- which walks the whole subprogram body exactly once, strictly after both fixed-point passes have fully drained -- perform the same Proved_Safe/Definite_Error/Unproved determination for an identifier's initialization-check that the live, mid-fixed-point recording already did, but against the node's own fully-converged State and marked Final, so it always supersedes whatever a premature live recording left behind. Confirmed on the reduced fixture (now Unproved instead of Definite_Error) and on the real corpus: Tokeneer's msgproc.adb Definite_Error is gone, and the same fix additionally corrected 123 initialization-check obligations elsewhere in the corpus that were stuck at a spurious Proved_Safe from the same mechanism (1661 -> 1538 Proved_Safe, all 123 moving to the honest Unproved, not to Definite_Error), confirming the staleness bug ran in both directions, not just the alarming one. Full test suite (tests/run_all.sh, 19 suites including the GNATprove differential corpus) passes unchanged. Regression: tests/verification_loop_stale_initialization.adb, run by run_verification.sh, confirmed to report Definite_Error before this fix and Unproved after. The identical stickiness mechanism affects at least one other live recording site (Interpret_Proof_Pragma's assertion-check, observed on Tokeneer's enrolment.adb "pragma Loop_Invariant (CertNo >= 2);" at :239) and was deliberately left open as FP-032, rather than folded into this fix, since correcting it requires the same Final treatment plus re-deriving the VC/symbolic-prover-aware assertion result Finalize_Node does not currently compute, not just a parameter default.

The same Register_At staleness mechanism fixed for initialization-check in FP-031 (and Range_Check/Index_Check/Division_By_Zero_Check/Integer_Overflow_Check in FP-034..FP-037) also affected Interpret_Proof_Pragma's live assertion-check recording (used for both plain pragma Assert and pragma Loop_Invariant/Loop_Variant conditions): a Definite_Error or Proved_Safe recorded from an intermediate, not-yet-converged CFG state during Verify_Subprogram's live Process_Node processing was not corrected by a later, fully-converged recording for the same stable ID, because Finalize_Node's own Pragma_Node handling only ever called the coarse Final_Outcome fallback (Unsupported/Unreachable/Unproved only; it never re-derived Proved_Safe or Definite_Error). Fixed the same way as FP-034..FP-037: the assertion-determination logic inside Interpret_Proof_Pragma was factored out into Check_Proof_Pragma_Assertion (Unit, Cond, State, Symbols, Final), called from Interpret_Proof_Pragma unchanged (Final defaulting False) and from a new Finalize_Assertion_Check helper in Verify_Subprogram's Finalize_Node, which replays it against the converged State/Symbolic_State with Final => True -- superseding Finalize_Node's previous Final_Outcome-only fallback for Proof.Assertion_Check, the same way Finalize_Range_Check etc. already did for their own kinds. Unlike Check_Value_Range and friends, Interpret_Proof_Pragma itself also runs Scan_Expression_For_Flow_Bugs and a state-narrowing step for live execution; both were deliberately left out of the extracted, replayable core so the replay has no side effects beyond the one recording it exists to correct. Reproduced with a fixture in FP-034's exact shape: "Val : Integer := 0; for I in 1 .. Arg loop Val := 5; end loop; pragma Assert (Val <= 2);" -- before the fix, the pragma Assert was recorded Proved_Safe (only the pre-loop Val = 0 visible on the CFG fixed point's first visit to the statement after the loop); after, correctly Unproved; confirmed both directions by toggling the fix and re-running (proved-safe before, unproved after, identical stable ID). Full test suite (tests/run_all.sh) passes unchanged. Regression: tests/verification_loop_stale_assert.adb, run by run_verification.sh. The originally-reported real-corpus case (AdaCore/spark2014 Tokeneer, enrolment.adb's "pragma Loop_Invariant (CertNo >= 2);" at :239) could not be used to confirm the fix in this environment: without a GNAT toolchain on PATH (gnatls; see FP-029), that file's semantic resolution differs enough that the same obligation already reports Unproved via a different method (static-evaluation vs. abstract-interpretation) regardless of this fix, so no before/after delta was observable there -- the synthetic fixture is the controlling evidence instead. FP-033 (Precondition_Check) remains open, same mechanism, different obligation kind.

The same Register_At staleness mechanism fixed for initialization-check (FP-031), Range_Check/Index_Check/Division_By_Zero_Check/Integer_Overflow_Check (FP-034..FP-037), and Assertion_Check (FP-032) also affected Precondition_Check, recorded by Check_Call_Precondition. It was reachable live from Process_Node's Ada_Call_Stmt handling ("Check_Call_Precondition (Unit, Source.As_Call_Stmt.F_Call, Input, Input_Symbols);") and again from Scan_Expression_For_Flow_Bugs's own Ada_Call_Expr case, both passing the CFG node's current, not-necessarily-converged Input state into Boolean_Value/VC.Decide against the callee's substituted precondition. Fixed the same way as FP-032: Check_Call_Precondition gained a Final parameter (default False, threaded to its Record_Definite_Error/Record_Proved_Safe/Record_Unproved calls only), and a new Finalize_Precondition_Check helper in Verify_Subprogram's Finalize_Node replays it against the converged State/Symbolic_State with Final => True, superseding the previous Final_Outcome-only fallback. One complication beyond FP-032's design, discovered while implementing rather than during the original audit: the two live sites above record under two genuinely different stable IDs for the same call, not one -- Process_Node's own Ada_Call_Stmt handling passes the whole call (Source.As_Call_Stmt.F_Call, e.g. "Helper (Val)", with the full symbolic state), while Scan_Expression_For_Flow_Bugs's generic recursion independently reaches the same Call_Expr node moments later and records again under just the callee name (Call.F_Name, e.g. "Helper", without symbols) -- confirmed empirically: a single call with a Pre contract produces two separate "precondition"-kind proof obligations in --verify's JSON output, one per span, both susceptible to the staleness bug independently. Finalize_Precondition_Check therefore replays Check_Call_Precondition twice per visited call node, once against Call and once against Call.F_Name, so both stable IDs are corrected; fixing only one (as a naive port of FP-032's single-replay pattern would have) would have left the other permanently unfinalized rather than merely stale, a strictly worse outcome the original FP-033 note did not anticipate. Reproduced with a fixture in FP-034's shape: "procedure Helper (X : Integer) with SPARK_Mode, Global => null, Pre => X <= 2; Val : Integer := 0; for I in 1 .. Arg loop Val := 5; end loop; Helper (Val);" -- before the fix, both "Helper (Val)" and "Helper" obligations were recorded Proved_Safe (only the pre-loop Val = 0 visible on the CFG fixed point's first visit); after, both correctly Unproved; confirmed both directions by toggling the fix. Full test suite (tests/run_all.sh) passes unchanged. Regression: tests/verification_loop_stale_precondition.adb, run by run_verification.sh. As anticipated by the original audit, the real Tokeneer corpus could not confirm this fix either way: re-running --verify across the whole corpus finds zero precondition-check obligations at all (no call in the corpus both carries a Pre contract and resolves under Effective_SPARK_Enabled the way this analyzer requires), so the synthetic fixture is the only evidence, as it was for FP-032.

The same Register_At staleness mechanism fixed for initialization-check in FP-031 also affected Range_Check, recorded by Check_Value_Range. It is reachable live from Interpret_Statement's Ada_Assign_Stmt case (itself called from Process_Node for every assignment statement), from Transfer_Declaration for object-declaration default expressions, and from Check_Conversion_Or_Index's Type_Conversion case, all evaluating Definitely_Outside_Type/Definitely_Inside_Type against the CFG node's current, not-necessarily-converged State. Reduced to a fixture demonstrating the dangerous direction directly (a false safety claim, not just a false alarm): "Val : Integer := 0; for I in 1 .. Arg loop Val := 5; end loop; V2 := Val;" where V2's subtype is "range 0 .. 2" -- before the fix, the range-check on "V2 := Val" was recorded proved-safe, because the CFG fixed point's first visit to that statement (before the loop's back edge propagates) sees only Val's pre-loop value of 0, which is inside 0..2; the converged state (Val could be 0 or 5) is neither definitely inside nor outside 0..2, so the honest answer is unproved. Confirmed on real code: re-running Tokeneer's --verify, range-check's Proved_Safe count fell from 105 to 102, all three moving to Unproved (not Definite_Error); Definite_Error stayed at 1 (FP-032's unrelated, still-open enrolment.adb case). Fixed the same way as FP-031: Check_Value_Range gained a Final parameter (default False, threaded to its Record_Definite_Error/Record_Proved_Safe/Record_Unproved calls only -- its Typ-unresolved branch is state-independent and did not need it), and Verify_Subprogram's Finalize_Node gained Finalize_Range_Check, a small helper mirroring Final_Outcome's Boundary_Supported/Reachable guard but replaying Check_Value_Range itself (Typ re-derived the same way each of the three live call sites derives it) against the converged State with Final => True, for all three Range_Check shapes (Ada_Assign_Stmt, Ada_Object_Decl, Type_Conversion). Report_Rule_Violation needed no special handling on the replay: FP-038's Already_Reported deduplication, fixed just before this, already makes a repeated call for the same (file, line, column, rule, message) a no-op. Full test suite (tests/run_all.sh) passes unchanged. Regression: tests/verification_loop_stale_range.adb, run by run_verification.sh, confirmed to report the assignment's range-check as proved-safe before this fix and unproved after.

The same Register_At staleness mechanism fixed for Range_Check in FP-034 also affected Index_Check, recorded by Check_Conversion_Or_Index's Array_Index case. Fixed the same way: the check's core logic was factored out into Check_Index_Range (Unit, Index_Value, Bounds, State, Final), called both from the live site (Final defaulting False, unchanged behavior) and from a new Finalize_Index_Check helper in Verify_Subprogram's Finalize_Node, which re-derives Array_Type/Bounds the same way the live site does and replays Check_Index_Range against the converged State with Final => True -- superseding Finalize_Node's previous Final_Outcome-only fallback, which could never produce Proved_Safe/Definite_Error to correct a stuck live result. Reproduced with a fixture in FP-034's shape: "Idx : Integer := 0; for I in 1 .. Arg loop Idx := 5; end loop; V2 := Arr (Idx);" on a 3-element array -- before the fix, the index-check on "Arr (Idx)" was proved-safe (only the pre-loop Idx = 0 was visible on the CFG fixed point's first visit); after, correctly unproved. Confirmed on real code: re-running Tokeneer's --verify, index-check counts were unchanged (no case in the corpus happened to hit the staleness window), a useful negative data point distinct from FP-034's positive one. Regression: tests/verification_loop_stale_index.adb, run by run_verification.sh.

The same Register_At staleness mechanism fixed for Range_Check in FP-034 also affected Division_By_Zero_Check, recorded by Scan_Expression_For_Flow_Bugs's Ada_Bin_Op case for "/", "mod", and "rem". Fixed the same way: the check's core logic was factored out into Check_Division_By_Zero (Unit, Expr, State, Final), called both from the live site (Final defaulting False) and from a new Finalize_Division_Check helper in Finalize_Node, replaying it against the converged State with Final => True. Reproduced with a fixture in FP-034's shape: "Divisor : Integer := 5; for I in 1 .. Arg loop Divisor := 0; end loop; Result := 100 / Divisor;" -- before the fix, the division-by-zero check was proved-safe ("right operand range excludes zero", based only on the pre-loop Divisor = 5 visible on the CFG fixed point's first visit); after, correctly unproved. Confirmed on real code: re-running Tokeneer's --verify, division-by-zero counts were unchanged (no case in the corpus happened to hit the staleness window). Regression: tests/verification_loop_stale_division.adb, run by run_verification.sh.

The same Register_At staleness mechanism fixed for Range_Check in FP-034 also affected Integer_Overflow_Check, recorded alongside FP-036 in Scan_Expression_For_Flow_Bugs's Ada_Bin_Op case, for "+", "-", "*", "/", and "**". Fixed the same way: the check's core logic was factored out into Check_Integer_Overflow (Unit, Node, State, Final), called both from the live site and from a new Finalize_Overflow_Check helper in Finalize_Node, replaying it against the converged State with Final => True. Reproduced with a fixture in FP-034's shape: "X : Integer := 0; for I in 1 .. Arg loop X := Integer'Last; end loop; Y := X + 1;" -- before the fix, the overflow check on "X + 1" was proved-safe (only the pre-loop X = 0 visible on the fixed point's first visit, giving a result of 1, comfortably in range); after, correctly unproved. Confirmed on real code: re-running Tokeneer's --verify, integer-overflow's Proved_Safe count fell from 13 to 6, with 3 moving to the honest Unproved and 4 disappearing entirely -- those 4 were phantom obligations Finalize_Node's old, unconditional Final_Outcome call created for Bin_Op nodes whose Expr_Type never resolved to an integer type, which the live site's own guard (mirrored exactly by Check_Integer_Overflow) would never have created an obligation for in the first place; Definite_Error stayed at 1, FP-032's still-open, unrelated enrolment.adb case. Regression: tests/verification_loop_stale_overflow.adb, run by run_verification.sh.

Discovered while designing FP-034's fix, a distinct bug from the Register_At staleness family (FP-031/032/033-037): Report.Report_Violation_At, the ordinary-findings counterpart to Register_At, had no deduplication at all -- Findings is a flat vector appended to unconditionally on every call. Every "Known_*" verify-mode rule (Known_Range_Check_Failure, Known_Overflow_Failure, Known_Index_Check_Failure, Known_Precondition_Failure, Known_Postcondition_Failure, Known_Assertion_Failure, non-static Division_By_Zero) calls Report_Rule_Violation from inside the same live functions Verify_Subprogram's CFG fixed point can call more than once for the identical AST node while converging (the FP-031 mechanism); when the violation stayed genuinely true across re-visits, as a real one usually would, it was reported once per re-visit instead of once. Reproduced with a fixture reusing FP-031's exact shape ("for I in 1 .. Arg loop Unrelated := I; end loop; Val := 999;", Val's subtype excluding 999): "Violations : 5" for what should be 2 (one Dead_Store, one Known_Range_Check_Failure), with the range-check warning printed four times for the identical statement. A second, structurally unrelated root cause surfaced during real-corpus verification: Checks.Report_Non_Short_Circuit_Operators recurses into every nested Bin_Op of a chained "and"/"or" expression, and Libadalang gives every node in a left-associative chain the same Sloc_Range.Start (the leftmost operand's position), so a chain of N plain "and"/"or" operators was reported N-1 times at the identical location regardless of --verify; found live in AdaCore/spark2014's Tokeneer corpus, clock.adb:113:10's 10-term range-guard "and" chain, reported 9 times instead of once. Confirmed on the real corpus: Tokeneer's --recommended --spark violation count fell from 652 to 631 (all 21 in Non_Short_Circuit_Condition; --verify's proof-obligation counts were unaffected, since Register_At's own status-equality check already no-ops an identical repeated recording -- only Report_Violation_At's unconditional append lacked this). Fixed by adding Already_Reported, a linear scan of Findings for a matching (Filename, Line_Number, Column, Rule, Message) tuple, checked at the top of Report_Violation_At before Consume_Baseline_Occurrence runs (so a suppressed duplicate call cannot also consume a baseline slot); the check is intentionally narrower than Stable_Fingerprint's own (Filename, Rule_Name, Message, Source_Text) key, since quality/README.md documents that duplicate fingerprints across genuinely different locations are intended to remain distinct, countable findings for baseline purposes. recommended.baseline (plain --recommended) is unaffected, since Non_Short_Circuit_Condition is only enabled by the --spark/--automotive/--do178c presets. Regressions: tests/verification_loop_stale_range_check.adb (run_verification.sh, the CFG-revisit shape) and tests/non_short_circuit_chain_findings.adb (run_bug_findings.sh, the chained-operator shape), both confirmed to report the duplicated count before this fix and the correct count after.

--verify's initialization-check recorded Definite_Error for a scalar named only in a nested subprogram declaration's Global aspect (e.g. "procedure Quarter_Rounds with Global => (In_Out => (x0, ..., x15));", a spec-only forward declaration, body given later), even though naming an object in a Global aspect is a contract, never an executable read at that textual position; the object's real initializing assignment, later in the enclosing subprogram's own statement list, was never reached because the check had already misfired against the aspect text. Root cause: Finalize_Node's generic recursive fallback in flow_interp.adb, which walks a subprogram's whole body a second time after the CFG fixed point converges to emit final proof-obligation outcomes, only excluded recursion into a nested Ada_Subp_Body (the FP-017 fix, for a different bug); it had no exclusion for Ada_Aspect_Spec, so it walked straight into a nested Ada_Subp_Decl's Global aspect expression and classified each named identifier via the same Initialization_Read_Required path an ordinary read would use. The CFG position used to look up flow state for that occurrence came from Matching_CFG_Node, which only matches nodes that are themselves the Source of a CFG node; CFG.Build_Declarations assigns exactly one CFG node per declarative-part child regardless of decl kind, so the whole nested declaration -- Global aspect included -- shares one CFG position, positioned in program order before the real assignments in the enclosing body's statements, where the object was still Bool_False (uninitialized). Pre and Post aspects do not share this exposure: they are extracted explicitly via Contract_Expression and scanned through the separate Scan_Expression_For_Flow_Bugs path (correct, since a precondition or postcondition is a genuinely-evaluated expression), which is never handed a whole declarative part and so never reaches a sibling declaration's aspects; Depends is not special-cased anywhere either and would likely share Global's exposure if used, though the confirmed repro is Global specifically. Found while building a project-scale precision/recall benchmark against GNATprove on rod-chapman/SPARKnaCl (see benchmarks/sparknacl/): every one of AdaLang's 48 Definite_Error verdicts on the whole corpus was this exact bug at one location, sparknacl-core.adb's ChaCha20_Encrypt_Bytes, where three nested procedures (Quarter_Rounds, Assign_X_To, Update_Xs) each name the same 16 state variables x0..x15 in Global aspects preceding their real initialization (16 variables, 3 declarations, minus overlap = 48 flagged occurrences); GNATprove proves the corpus fully, giving zero support for any of the 48. Fixed by returning immediately from Finalize_Node when Node.Kind = Ada_Aspect_Spec, before the generic child-recursion loop, so no aspect specification's expression tree -- Global's or otherwise -- is ever walked as executable code by this pass. Confirmed on the real corpus: SPARKNaCl's --verify Definite_Error count fell from 48 to 0 (Proved_Safe rose slightly, from 3454 to 3457, as a handful of downstream obligations that had been poisoned by the bogus reads now resolve cleanly). Regression: tests/verification_global_aspect_reference_clean.adb (the exact SPARKNaCl shape, must show no Definite_Error) and tests/verification_global_aspect_reference_guard.adb (a genuine uninitialized read of an unrelated variable in the enclosing subprogram's own statements, near the same Global-aspect shape, must still be flagged), both run by run_verification.sh.

--verify's proof-obligation finalization pass (Verify_Subprogram's Finalize_Node, in flow_interp.adb) could abort the whole file instead of just skipping one obligation, whenever a Libadalang property it called directly -- Node.As_Call_Expr.P_Kind, P_Expression_Type, or P_Designated_Type_Decl -- raised Property_Error. Root-caused with a minimal, AUnit-free, two-project reproduction (a project Main withing a separate project Dep via with "dep/dep.gpr"; a procedure in Main calling any subprogram declared in Dep, regardless of its signature or return type) and a symbolic backtrace (temporary GNAT.Traceback.Symbolic instrumentation in Process_File, reverted): CallExpr.P_Kind's own logic (Name.is_call, is_array_slice, an array/user-defined-indexing check, then a Type_Conversion/Family_Index check via Name.referenced_decl with Imprecise_Fallback => False) falls through to "raise Property_Error with 'undetermined CallExpr kind'" once Name.is_call's own called_formal_subp_spec dispatcher returns null for a call whose callee is declared in a separate, with'd GNAT project -- confirmed independent of return type, of whether the callee's project is a library project, and of generics; a single-project control with byte-identical source compiled cleanly. This is an upstream Libadalang precise-resolution limitation, not an AdaLang Analyzer logic error, and there is no way to make CallExpr.P_Kind itself succeed from this side of the boundary (the same category as FP-029, though a different property and a different trigger: FP-029 needs gnatls missing from PATH; this needs nothing but an ordinary cross-project call, and gnatls was confirmed present throughout every reproduction). What was fixable, and is what this entry closes, is the blast radius: Finalize_Node called Call.P_Kind a second time directly inside an if-condition ("if Node.Kind = Ada_Call_Expr and then Node.As_Call_Expr.P_Kind = Call then"), outside the begin/exception block a few lines below it, so a Property_Error there escaped Finalize_Node entirely and propagated through its own recursive child-walk, Verify_Subprogram, and Verify_Unit to Process_File's outer handler, aborting the whole file instead of just this one call's obligations. A second, structurally identical gap covered several sibling branches (Ada_Bin_Op_Range, Ada_Assign_Stmt, Ada_Object_Decl, Ada_Pragma_Node) that call P_Expression_Type or P_Designated_Type_Decl directly as argument expressions with no begin/exception block of their own at all; a second backtrace, captured the same way against the real cubesatlab/cubedos corpus, confirmed Expr.P_Expression_Type escaping from the Ada_Assign_Stmt branch ("dereferencing a null access", a different Property_Error message than FP-040's original CallExpr.P_Kind signature, but the identical unguarded-direct-property-call shape). Fixed in two parts: (1) the second P_Kind check now evaluates into a local Is_Plain_Call flag inside its own begin/exception block first, falling back to False (the existing conservative raw-tree-recursion path) on failure instead of letting the condition's own evaluation raise; (2) the entire per-node dispatch if/elsif chain (all branches from Ada_Bin_Op_Range through the Ada_Identifier initialization-check case) is now wrapped in one outer begin/exception, reported via Report_Recoverable_Failure_Once under Operation "finalize node proof obligations", so any branch's own property access failing skips only that node's own obligations and still falls through to the child-recursion loop that keeps walking the rest of the file -- matching the conservative fallback philosophy the two originally-guarded branches (Ada_Call_Expr's case statement, Ada_Identifier's initialization case) already had. Confirmed on the real corpus: re-running --verify against cubesatlab/cubedos's unmodified src/cubedos.gpr, the 21-of-49-files whole-file aborts are gone (0 "Error processing" lines), and reported proof obligations rose from 44 to 680 (Proved_Safe 2 to 16, Unproved 9 to 8, Unsupported 33 to 583, plus 73 Unreachable now visible) -- see benchmarks/cubedos/RESULTS_2026-08-04.md for the full before/after comparison against GNATprove. Regression: tests/verification_cross_project/ (a two-project fixture: dep/dep.gpr's Dep_Pkg.Make called from verification_cross_project_clean.adb via main.gpr's "with 'dep/dep.gpr';"), run by run_verification.sh with an explicit -P (the only fixture in that file that needs one, since the bug only manifests across a real project boundary that a project-less bare-file run never exercises); the check asserts no "Error processing" line appears on stderr. Full test suite (tests/run_all.sh, all 19 suites including the GNATprove differential corpus and the quality-metrics gate) passes unchanged.

Non_Short_Circuit_Condition flags plain "and"/"or" inside an if/elsif/exit-when/while condition regardless of operand type, but its advice ("use 'and then'/'or else' instead") is only legal Ada for Boolean operands: RM 4.5.7 restricts the short-circuit forms to Boolean. Checks.Report_Non_Short_Circuit_Operators (checks.adb) matches purely on Bin_Op.F_Op = Ada_Op_And/Ada_Op_Or with no check of the operand type, so a bitwise "and"/"or" on a modular (or other non-Boolean) type inside a condition is misreported as a short-circuit-guard violation the developer cannot actually fix as suggested. Reproduced with a minimal fixture: "type Flags_Type is mod 256; Flags, Mask : Flags_Type; ... if (Flags and Mask) /= 0 then null; end if;" -- "adalang_analyzer -checks='-*,Non_Short_Circuit_Condition'" reports one violation on "Flags and Mask" with the message "use 'and then' instead of 'and' in a condition", which would not compile if applied. Found while extending the precision corpus (quality/precision_corpus.tsv) for a Non_Short_Circuit_Condition boundary case, not yet confirmed against a real corpus. No fixture checked in yet; not yet fixed. A fix would need Report_Non_Short_Circuit_Operators (or its Bin_Op case) to check the operator's operand type resolves to Standard.Boolean (mirroring Is_Standard_Boolean_Expression already used by Duplicate_Boolean_Operand/Contradictory_Condition in checks-expressions.adb) before reporting, and to conservatively skip -- not report -- when that type cannot be resolved. Fixed by adding Is_Standard_Boolean_Operand (checks.adb), mirroring Checks.Expressions.Is_Standard_Boolean_Expression, and gating Report_Non_Short_Circuit_Operators's Bin_Op case on the left operand's own resolved type being exactly Standard.Boolean before reporting; resolution failure is conservatively treated as "not Boolean" (skip, not report), the same fallback the mirrored function already uses. Confirmed on the reported repro (the modular "Flags and Mask" fixture, now clean) and confirmed the existing FP-038 chain regression (tests/non_short_circuit_chain_findings.adb, plain Boolean "and" operands) still fires exactly once, unaffected. A known, accepted narrowing: a derived Boolean type (e.g. "type Flag is new Boolean;") resolves to its own declaration, not "standard.boolean", so it no longer receives the suggestion either, a rare false negative traded for closing a false positive on the far more common modular/bitwise-flag shape, consistent with this project's conservative bias. Regression: tests/non_short_circuit_modular_clean.adb, run by run_bug_findings.sh (must stay clean under -checks='Non_Short_Circuit_Condition'); also folded into quality/precision_corpus.tsv as a negative-non-boolean-operand/boundary-boolean-operand pair. Full test suite (tests/run_all.sh) passes unchanged.
